name: text
text: Protocols, PHY waveforms, and the design choices behind 802.11b → be — plus the 60 GHz ad/ay branch
textPreview: Protocols, PHY waveforms, and the design choices behind 802.11b → be — plus the 60 GHz ad/ay branch

text:
• Open with a familiar question: why does the Wi‑Fi icon look unchanged while the radio underneath has changed repeatedly?
• The lecture follows two threads: historical standardization and the PHY resource dimensions used to gain capacity.

[Sources]
- https://standards.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/interactive/web/wi-fi-timeline/index.html
- https://extr-p-001.sitecorecontenthub.cloud/api/public/content/3f5d887b048d49cba95392b829960d1b?download=true&v=564c5124

name: slide-title
text: Wi‑Fi improved by spending new resource dimensions
textPreview: Wi‑Fi improved by spending new resource dimensions

text:
• Use this as the organizing framework for the whole lecture.
• Every later amendment keeps the core 802.11 family identity but adds one or more dimensions for peak rate, capacity, reliability, or latency.

[Sources]
- https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/802.11/10548/
- https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/802.11be/7516/
- https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/products/collateral/wireless/white-paper-c11-740788.html

name: slide-title
text: An amendment name and a Wi‑Fi generation are not the same thing
textPreview: An amendment name and a Wi‑Fi generation are not the same thing

text:
• Explain that IEEE names technical amendments; the Wi‑Fi Alliance later introduced simpler generation names.
• 802.11ad and 802.11ay are a parallel 60 GHz branch commonly associated with WiGig rather than the numbered Wi‑Fi 1–7 sequence.

[Sources]
- https://standards.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/interactive/web/wi-fi-timeline/index.html
- https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/802.11/10548/
- https://helpfiles.keysight.com/csg/n7637/Content/Main/802.11ad%20Concepts.htm

name: slide-title
text: Four milestones made consumer Wi‑Fi possible by 1999
textPreview: Four milestones made consumer Wi‑Fi possible by 1999

name: text
text: Wireless packet networking proves shared radio access.
textPreview: Wireless packet networking proves shared radio access.

name: text
text: FCC opens spectrum for spread-spectrum systems.
textPreview: FCC opens spectrum for spread-spectrum systems.

name: text
text: A common MAC/PHY standard replaces vendor islands.
textPreview: A common MAC/PHY standard replaces vendor islands.

text:
• Connect ALOHAnet to random access, then connect unlicensed spectrum to permissionless innovation.
• The 1997 base standard existed before the Wi‑Fi brand; 1999 is the commercial inflection point with 802.11a/b and interoperability certification.

[Sources]
- https://standards.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/interactive/web/wi-fi-timeline/index.html
- https://extr-p-001.sitecorecontenthub.cloud/api/public/content/3f5d887b048d49cba95392b829960d1b?download=true&v=564c5124

name: slide-title
text: The recognizable 802.11 protocol lives above changing PHYs
textPreview: The recognizable 802.11 protocol lives above changing PHYs

name: text
text: Preamble • header • rate signaling • PPDU format
textPreview: Preamble • header • rate signaling • PPDU format

name: text
text: DSSS • OFDM • MIMO • OFDMA • single carrier
textPreview: DSSS • OFDM • MIMO • OFDMA • single carrier

name: text
text: Different ways to turn bits into radio energy
textPreview: Different ways to turn bits into radio energy

text:
• Define a PPDU as the PHY-layer transmission unit placed on air.
• The MAC delivers familiar behaviors across generations, while PLCP/PMD details define the preamble, coding, modulation, channel width, and spatial streams.

[Sources]
- https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/802.11/10548/

name: slide-title
text: The 1997 baseline solved shared access before it solved speed
textPreview: The 1997 baseline solved shared access before it solved speed

name: text
text: Listen → wait → random backoff → transmit → ACK
textPreview: Listen → wait → random backoff → transmit → ACK

name: text
text: CSMA/CA avoids collisions; it cannot detect them while transmitting.
textPreview: CSMA/CA avoids collisions; it cannot detect them while transmitting.

text:
• Contrast Ethernet collision detection with wireless collision avoidance.
• A station may not hear every other station, and its own transmission overwhelms the receiver; hence carrier sense, random backoff, positive ACK, and optional RTS/CTS.

[Sources]
- https://standards.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/interactive/web/wi-fi-timeline/index.html
- https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/802.11/10548/

name: slide-title
text: 802.11b made 2.4 GHz practical with coded spreading
textPreview: 802.11b made 2.4 GHz practical with coded spreading

name: text
text: One symbol becomes a patterned chip sequence
textPreview: One symbol becomes a patterned chip sequence

name: text
text: CCK encodes information in the phase relationships of code words; spreading provides processing gain and robustness.
textPreview: CCK encodes information in the phase relationships of code words; spreading provides processing gain and robustness.

text:
• Start with 802.11b because DSSS is intuitive: replace each symbol with a longer chip pattern.
• Avoid saying that CCK merely repeats bits. It selects complex code words whose phases carry multiple bits while preserving useful correlation properties.
• The familiar three non-overlapping 2.4 GHz channels in North America arise because the occupied channels are much wider than their 5 MHz center spacing.

[Sources]
- https://standards.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/interactive/web/wi-fi-timeline/index.html
- https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/802.11/10548/

name: slide-title
text: 802.11a replaced spreading with many orthogonal subcarriers
textPreview: 802.11a replaced spreading with many orthogonal subcarriers

name: text
text: OFDM spectrum: overlapping subcarriers, orthogonal at sampling points
textPreview: OFDM spectrum: overlapping subcarriers, orthogonal at sampling points

text:
• Explain orthogonality operationally: each subcarrier is sampled where the others cross zero, allowing spectra to overlap without ideal inter-carrier interference.
• The cyclic prefix converts multipath delay spread into a manageable guard interval and supports simple frequency-domain equalization.
• 802.11a reached 54 Mb/s but early 5 GHz propagation and device cost slowed mass adoption relative to 802.11b.

[Sources]
- https://standards.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/interactive/web/wi-fi-timeline/index.html
- https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/802.11/10548/

name: slide-title
text: 802.11g brought the 802.11a waveform back to 2.4 GHz
textPreview: 802.11g brought the 802.11a waveform back to 2.4 GHz

name: text
text: Backward-compatible mixed networks pay protection overhead when legacy 802.11b stations are present.
textPreview: Backward-compatible mixed networks pay protection overhead when legacy 802.11b stations are present.

text:
• Frame 802.11g as a strategic recombination: the OFDM PHY ideas of 802.11a in the popular 2.4 GHz ecosystem.
• Backward compatibility accelerated adoption but created mixed-mode protection overhead.

[Sources]
- https://standards.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/interactive/web/wi-fi-timeline/index.html
- https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/802.11/10548/

name: slide-title
text: 802.11n scales rate in bandwidth, space, and time
textPreview: 802.11n scales rate in bandwidth, space, and time

name: text
text: Antenna arrays turn multipath from an impairment into parallel spatial streams.
textPreview: Antenna arrays turn multipath from an impairment into parallel spatial streams.

text:
• 802.11n is the major architectural jump: MIMO, channel bonding, short guard interval, and aggregation work together.
• Maximum standardized configuration reaches 600 Mb/s using four spatial streams, 40 MHz, 64-QAM 5/6, and short GI; typical client devices implement fewer streams.

[Sources]
- https://standards.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/interactive/web/wi-fi-timeline/index.html
- https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/docs/wireless-mobility/wireless-lan-wlan/212892-802-11ac-wireless-throughput-testing-and.html

name: slide-title
text: 802.11ac pushes the 5 GHz OFDM formula harder
textPreview: 802.11ac pushes the 5 GHz OFDM formula harder

text:
• Summarize 802.11ac with Cisco's memorable dimensions: wider channels, tighter modulation, more spatial streams, and downlink MU-MIMO.
• 256-QAM carries 8 coded bits per subcarrier symbol but requires higher SNR than 64-QAM.
• Maximum PHY rates are configuration ceilings, not expected application throughput.

[Sources]
- https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/wireless/controller/technotes/8-4/b_cisco_aironet_series_migrating_to802_11_ac.html
- https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/docs/wireless-mobility/wireless-lan-wlan/212892-802-11ac-wireless-throughput-testing-and.html

name: slide-title
text: 802.11ax optimizes dense efficiency, not only peak speed
textPreview: 802.11ax optimizes dense efficiency, not only peak speed

name: text
text: Before: one user occupies the channel
textPreview: Before: one user occupies the channel

name: text
text: 802.11ax: users share frequency in one PPDU
textPreview: 802.11ax: users share frequency in one PPDU

text:
• OFDMA is the conceptual center: an AP partitions OFDM subcarriers into resource units for multiple stations in the same transmission opportunity.
• 802.11ax adds frequency as a multiuser allocation dimension on top of time and space.
• The design target is high efficiency in dense deployments, not simply a larger single-link headline rate.

[Sources]
- https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/products/collateral/wireless/white-paper-c11-740788.html
- https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/802.11/10548/

name: text
text: 4× more FFT points in the same 20 MHz channel
textPreview: 4× more FFT points in the same 20 MHz channel

name: text
text: Longer symbols improve tolerance to delay spread and create finer-grained resource units; guard intervals adapt to the environment.
textPreview: Longer symbols improve tolerance to delay spread and create finer-grained resource units; guard intervals adapt to the environment.

text:
• For a 20 MHz channel, legacy OFDM uses 312.5 kHz subcarrier spacing and 3.2 μs useful symbol time; HE OFDM uses 78.125 kHz and 12.8 μs.
• A longer OFDM symbol reduces the relative cost of a longer guard interval and creates more subcarriers that can be grouped into resource units.
• The diagram is conceptual and not a literal spectrum mask.

[Sources]
- https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/products/collateral/wireless/white-paper-c11-740788.html

name: slide-title
text: Wi‑Fi 6E adds spectrum, not a new 802.11 waveform
textPreview: Wi‑Fi 6E adds spectrum, not a new 802.11 waveform

name: text
text: New operating spectrum and channel plan
textPreview: New operating spectrum and channel plan

name: text
text: A band extension is not the same as a new IEEE amendment.
textPreview: A band extension is not the same as a new IEEE amendment.

text:
• Clarify the naming trap: Wi‑Fi 6E is Wi‑Fi 6 / 802.11ax extended into 6 GHz; it is not a separate PHY generation.
• Regulatory channel availability varies by country, so avoid implying identical 6 GHz allocations worldwide.

[Sources]
- https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/802.11/10548/
- https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/docs/wireless-mobility/wireless-lan-wlan/212892-802-11ac-wireless-throughput-testing-and.html

name: slide-title
text: 802.11be makes several links behave like one connection
textPreview: 802.11be makes several links behave like one connection

text:
• MLO lets a device establish and coordinate links across bands; implementations can use links for throughput, load balancing, redundancy, or latency reduction.
• 802.11be adds 320 MHz channels, 4096-QAM, flexible puncturing, and other enhancements while preserving backward compatibility.
• IEEE 802.11be-2024 requires at least one mode supporting at least 30 Gb/s at the MAC service access point; marketing peak PHY figures may be higher.

[Sources]
- https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/802.11be/7516/
- https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/802.11/10548/

• 802.11ad is the Directional Multi-Gigabit branch around 60 GHz.
• Its 2.16 GHz-wide channels make multi-gigabit rates possible without relying only on extremely dense modulation.
• High path and penetration loss shrink coverage but enable directional reuse; beam training aligns transmit and receive sectors.

[Sources]
- https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/802.11/10548/
- https://helpfiles.keysight.com/csg/n7637/Content/Main/802.11ad%20Concepts.htm
- https://www.keysight.com/us/en/assets/7018-03292/application-notes/5990-9697.pdf

textPreview: 802.11ay turns the 60 GHz link into a wider, spatial system

name: text
text: 60 GHz evolves from a cable-replacement idea toward high-capacity access and backhaul.
textPreview: 60 GHz evolves from a cable-replacement idea toward high-capacity access and backhaul.

text:
• 802.11ay enhances operation in license-exempt bands above 45 GHz and requires at least one mode delivering at least 20 Gb/s at the MAC service access point.
• Key extensions include channel bonding/aggregation, MIMO, improved beamforming, and longer-range use cases.

[Sources]
- https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/802.11/10548/
- https://standards.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/import/documents/other/geps_07-iot_smart_cities.pdf

name: slide-title
text: Four waveform ideas explain most of Wi‑Fi’s PHY history
textPreview: Four waveform ideas explain most of Wi‑Fi’s PHY history

name: text
text: Waveform choice follows the channel: interference, delay spread, bandwidth, mobility, and hardware constraints.
textPreview: Waveform choice follows the channel: interference, delay spread, bandwidth, mobility, and hardware constraints.

text:
• Use this slide for retrieval practice: ask students to match standards to waveform families.
• DSSS/CCK: 802.11b. OFDM: 802.11a/g/n/ac and the basis of ax/be. OFDMA: multiuser extension emphasized by ax/be. 60 GHz single carrier: widely used in ad and enhanced by ay.
• The sketches are conceptual, not calibrated time-domain or spectrum-mask plots.

[Sources]
- https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/802.11/10548/
- https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/products/collateral/wireless/white-paper-c11-740788.html
- https://helpfiles.keysight.com/csg/n7637/Content/Main/802.11ad%20Concepts.htm

name: slide-title
text: The mainstream branch evolves continuously from b to be
textPreview: The mainstream branch evolves continuously from b to be

name: text
text: * 6 GHz via Wi‑Fi 6E certification / regulation.  † IEEE 802.11be requirement is measured at the MAC SAP.
textPreview: * 6 GHz via Wi‑Fi 6E certification / regulation.  † IEEE 802.11be requirement is measured at the MAC SAP.

text:
• Treat the maxima as comparison anchors, not promised throughput.
• The years are standard milestones; commercial availability and Wi‑Fi certification dates can differ.
• The standards allow configurations beyond what typical phones and access points implement.

[Sources]
- https://standards.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/interactive/web/wi-fi-timeline/index.html
- https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/802.11/10548/
- https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/802.11be/7516/
- https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/docs/wireless-mobility/wireless-lan-wlan/212892-802-11ac-wireless-throughput-testing-and.html

name: slide-title
text: A PHY rate is the product of several optimistic choices
textPreview: A PHY rate is the product of several optimistic choices

name: text
text: Application throughput is always lower—and depends on distance, interference, clients, and scheduler behavior.
textPreview: Application throughput is always lower—and depends on distance, interference, clients, and scheduler behavior.

text:
• Use this slide to inoculate students against comparing standards only by their maximum PHY rate.
• Wider bandwidth and higher QAM require suitable spectrum and SNR; more spatial streams require antennas and favorable channels; multiuser gains require traffic from multiple users.
• Ask which factor fails first when moving farther from the access point.

[Sources]
- https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/docs/wireless-mobility/wireless-lan-wlan/212892-802-11ac-wireless-throughput-testing-and.html
- https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/wireless/controller/technotes/8-4/b_cisco_aironet_series_migrating_to802_11_ac.html

name: slide-title
text: The MAC and security story evolves alongside the waveform
textPreview: The MAC and security story evolves alongside the waveform

name: text
text: PHY innovation changes what is possible; MAC innovation determines who gets airtime and how safely.
textPreview: PHY innovation changes what is possible; MAC innovation determines who gets airtime and how safely.

text:
• Keep security chronology high level: WEP's weaknesses motivated WPA as a transition and 802.11i/WPA2 as a durable redesign; WPA3 strengthens authentication and protection.
• Aggregation was essential because faster PHYs otherwise expose fixed per-frame overhead.
• MLO is both a PHY/MAC coordination story: multiple links must be discovered, negotiated, and scheduled.

[Sources]
- https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/802.11/10548/
- https://extr-p-001.sitecorecontenthub.cloud/api/public/content/3f5d887b048d49cba95392b829960d1b?download=true&v=564c5124
- https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/802.11be/7516/

name: slide-title
text: Wi‑Fi and cellular optimize different edges of the same network
textPreview: Wi‑Fi and cellular optimize different edges of the same network

name: text
text: Future edge systems choose, combine, and hand off across both.
textPreview: Future edge systems choose, combine, and hand off across both.

text:
• Relate the Wi‑Fi history back to Future Edge Networks.
• Avoid a winner/loser framing: Wi‑Fi excels at locally owned, high-capacity access; cellular excels at managed wide-area mobility. Modern devices and edge services use both.
• Invite examples: campus offload, AR/VR, industrial links, fixed wireless access, and multi-access edge computing.

[Sources]
- https://standards.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/import/documents/other/geps_07-iot_smart_cities.pdf

name: slide-title
text: Read any new Wi‑Fi generation through five questions
textPreview: Read any new Wi‑Fi generation through five questions

name: text
text: What does one PPDU look like?
textPreview: What does one PPDU look like?

name: text
text: What channel conditions does it assume?
textPreview: What channel conditions does it assume?

name: text
text: b → a/g → n → ac → ax → be
textPreview: b → a/g → n → ac → ax → be

text:
• Close by asking students to apply the five questions to one generation not emphasized in class.
• Suggested check: Why can 4096-QAM increase peak rate but reduce robustness? Why can OFDMA improve efficiency without changing the total channel bandwidth? Why is 60 GHz directional?
• The durable lesson is not memorizing letters; it is recognizing the resource dimension and engineering tradeoff each amendment introduces.

[Sources]
- https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/802.11/10548/
- https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/802.11be/7516/
